summary: In a major milestone for European commercial spaceflight, Germany’s Isar Aerospace has launched a rocket into orbit from Norway. In other launch operations, SpaceX successfully orbited 27 Starlink satellites aboard a Falcon 9 rocket before executing a landing on a drone ship at sea. On the civil space front, NASA is expanding its Deep Space Network infrastructure with a new dish in the California desert, as a new report evaluates funding for the agency’s Planetary Research and Analysis Programs. Internationally, European policy discussions emphasize the need for integrated cooperation among the Galileo, Copernicus, Cleansky, and IRIS² programs to maintain competitive standing in orbit. Defense and security developments also advanced as Sweden signed a HIMARS agreement and forged a rocket artillery pact with Finland, while Rafael, Lower Saxony, and Aurelius partnered to develop a former Volkswagen site in Germany. In astronomical research, the DESI legacy imaging survey released the largest 2D map of the universe to date, alongside the 20th data release from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey. Meanwhile, new theoretical models suggest Earth's moon may have formed in just five hours following a giant impact, and researchers developed a framework to measure the economic risks solar storms pose to the U.S. power grid. Looking ahead, skywatchers should prepare for September 8, when the moon will hide Jupiter in a rare daylight occultation.
